name: Rikkunshito (Kampo formula)
short: Case report: an extremely low birth weight infant developed persistent low potassium and metabolic alkalosis on rikkunshito (attributed to licorice). Trials reported no severe adverse events.
text: A 2026 case report describes an extremely low birth weight infant with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease who developed persistent hypokalaemia (low blood potassium) and metabolic alkalosis after treatment with rikkunshito; these gradually resolved after rikkunshito was stopped and potassium was given, and the authors suggest licorice-induced pseudoaldosteronism. A 2019 systematic review of 24 randomized trials (2175 participants) comparing rikkunshito with other treatments for upper gastrointestinal symptoms reported no drug-related severe adverse events, although most of the trials had high or unclear risk of bias. In an 8-week placebo-controlled trial in 247 people with functional dyspepsia there were no severe adverse events in either group; the abstract does not report milder events. In a crossover study in 8 healthy volunteers, a single dose of rikkunshito taken with the antibiotic levofloxacin did not significantly change levofloxacin's pharmacokinetics; no other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
